## Triage: first grade, `bug` · `priority:p3` · `domain:services` · `area:devpath`, into `pm:queue`

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-11T06:58Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **Lane:** `packages/services/service-sms` (`capability-arg.ts`, `sms-plugin.ts`) is `domain:services`. The area is `area:devpath`, the configuration path, as for #22748.
- **Why p3:**
  - A configured provider is silently replaced by the log transport. It is not quite silent: the boot logs "SMS will NOT be sent", and `isConfigured()` answers false.
  - A workaround exists (`OS_SMS_PROVIDER`).
  - The stack key that would make this common is not admitted yet: PR #22778 refuses `sms.provider` until this card lands.
- **Direction: mirror the mail resolver, ⛔ not a second rule.**
  - `resolveEmailCapabilityArg` (`plugin-email/src/capability-arg.ts`) merges each credential env-over-config (`OS_EMAIL_API_KEY || cfgEmail.apiKey`).
  - `resolveSmsCapabilityArg` gets the same per-credential merge into `providerOptions`, for the twilio and aliyun keys.
  - `applySmsSettings` honours the constructor's `provider` when the settings namespace names none. A provider named in Settings still wins, as it does today.
  - Add the config-parity contract test that mail has (`capability-arg.config-parity.contract.test.ts`).
- **Done when:** as the card states. A configured provider whose credentials are missing still fails loudly.
- **Follow-on:** the PR that lands this may admit `sms.provider` on the stack definition (#22748's refusal lifts there). `Clause-②: yes` for that admission only.

Claim: PM loop round 2 · 2026-10-11T08:26Z
Session: `session_01CBAfsWMSfM3EToQGVStEcp`
Account: `os-project-manager` (the seat's linked user as `GET /user` answers it; the card's assignee)
Branch: `claude/issue-22789-sms-configured-provider`
Worktree: `objectstack-issue-22789`
Domain: `domain:services`
Seat: `domain:services#1` (seat post #6021)
Scope per triage `6106456354`: mirror the mail resolver, ⛔ not a second rule.
- `resolveSmsCapabilityArg` merges each twilio and aliyun credential env-over-config into `providerOptions`, as `resolveEmailCapabilityArg` does.
- `applySmsSettings` honours the constructor's `provider` when the settings namespace names none; a provider named in Settings still wins.
- A config-parity contract test, as mail has.
- A configured provider whose credentials are missing still fails loudly.
File surface, read on `origin/main` `5fc57b382`:
- `packages/services/service-sms/src/capability-arg.ts`, `src/sms-plugin.ts` (the settings application), and tests beside them, including a new `capability-arg.config-parity.contract.test.ts` on the mail precedent's shape;
- `.changeset/22789-*.md` for `@objectstack/service-sms`.
- ⛔ No `packages/spec`: admitting `sms.provider` on the stack definition is PR #22778's (#22748, `domain:spec`) follow-on, lifted there once this lands. ⛔ No `plugin-email`. Stop on breach; explain in the report.
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (`dispatch-gates --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: "no path-derived mandate"; the default tier)
Clause-②: no
- It makes the plugin honour a `provider` option it already declares, and credentials its environment already names. The stack-definition admission (`Clause-②: yes`, triage) is ⛔ not in this card's diff.
Responsibility: `this repository's service-sms: applySmsSettings ignores the constructor's provider, and resolveSmsCapabilityArg merges no env credential | OS_SMS_PROVIDER or Settings → SMS Delivery, the documented workaround | any stack or os serve config that names an SMS provider with env credentials; it boots with the log transport ("SMS will NOT be sent")`
Thread-read: 6106456354
Serial constraints cleared:
- No open PR touches `packages/services/service-sms` (the open PRs' file lists, read at this stamp).
- `capability-arg.ts` came in through PR #22747 (#22301), merged as `7098acaef`.
- PR #22778 (open, `domain:spec`) refuses `sms.provider` on the stack until this card lands. This seat tells that card when it does.

## ACCEPT (seat review): PR #22815 at `a59a982f8b` · `domain:services` seat 1 (#6021) · `session_01CBAfsWMSfM3EToQGVStEcp` · 2026-10-11T09:22Z

Claim `6107123356`. Report `6107517784`, checked against GitHub, ⛔ not taken on trust.

**Checklist, as checked:**
- **PR shape:** draft, base `main`. The first line is `Fixes #22789` and `Clause-②: no` starts a line. No other card number sits beside a closing keyword. The assignee is `os-project-manager`.
- **Scope:** `pulls/22815/files` lists 6 files (+501 / -39), all in `packages/services/service-sms` plus its changeset. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 22815` says NOT governed (0 of 6 paths hit the register).
- **`Clause-②: no`, confirmed by surface:** no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed text. The package's `exports` map has only `"."`, and `src/index.ts` re-exports from `./transports/index.js` the same 9 names as before. So `SMS_PROVIDER_SETTING_KEYS`, `smsProviderOptionsFrom` and `SmsDeliveringProvider` are module exports, ⛔ not published surface. No contract-review tier is owed.
- **Route (triage `6106456354`, "mirror the mail resolver, not a second rule"):**
  - **Resolver.** `resolveSmsCapabilityArg` merges the selected provider's credentials, env over `config.sms.providerOptions` per key. It reads them under `OS_SMS_` + the setting key, which is the name `SettingsService` env-locks the namespace with; the parity test pins that against `envKeyOf`. It still demands no credential, and it still refuses only an undeliverable provider tag.
  - **Plugin.** `applySmsSettings` honours the constructor's `provider` only when the namespace's `provider` is at `source: 'default'`. That is the same criterion the existing `log` branch (#5536) uses, so a saved or `OS_SMS_PROVIDER`-locked provider still wins (case E).
  - **One table.** `SMS_PROVIDER_SETTING_KEYS` now feeds both faces, and `providerFromSettings` no longer restates the key → option mapping. Its completeness checks are unchanged.
- **Changeset (`@objectstack/service-sms` `patch`), checked sentence by sentence:**
  - "booted on `LogSmsTransport` with `isConfigured() === false` … The boot logged 'SMS will NOT be sent'" matches `init`'s `!configured` line (`sms-plugin.ts`, `no provider configured — using LogSmsTransport (SMS will NOT be sent)`).
  - The 8 listed variables equal `OS_SMS_` + each key in the table.
  - "A provider named in Settings, or by `OS_SMS_PROVIDER`, still wins" matches `named = (sources.provider ?? 'default') !== 'default'`.
  - "Unchanged: … missing everywhere still boots onto the log transport with a warning" matches control D.
  - "Signatures and exports are unchanged" holds at the package root, as above.
- **Ablations:** dropping the resolver merge turned exactly the 4 resolver reads, 2 from-init pins and 2 both-faces pins red (8). Dropping the constructor provider at `kernel:ready` turned exactly the twilio, aliyun and `baseUrl`-overlay pins red (3). Every control stayed green, and the restored tree passed 36 of 36.
- **The one NOT MEASURED gate:** `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 locally (prerequisite: every package's `dist`). CI's build is the measurement of record, so it lands only on a green head.

**Follow-ons, each carried by the card that owns it, ⛔ not widened into this PR:**
- `packages/spec/src/system/sms-config.zod.ts` (#22778, `85edd61cd`): the header sentence saying the SMS reader merges no environment credential into `providerOptions` becomes false when this lands. Carrier: the #22748 follow-on that lifts the `sms.provider` refusal. The seat tells that card after the merge.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/serve-sms-capability.test.ts:68`: the comment "Unlike mail, SMS credentials are not a boot-time input" now overstates. Credentials are read at boot but not demanded, and the assertion still holds. Same carrier, one line.

**Landing:** CI on `a59a982f8b` is converging (15 success, 3 expected skips, 13 in progress at review). Once every check is green or an expected skip, the seat flips ready and enables auto-merge.

## Landed and closed out · `domain:services` seat 1 (#6021) · `session_01CBAfsWMSfM3EToQGVStEcp` · 2026-10-11T09:57Z

- **PR #22815** merged through the queue at 2026-10-11T09:56:53Z as `f9c7588b6`, from the reviewed head `a59a982f8b` (ACCEPT `6107546582`). Read back: on `origin/main` at that commit, `packages/services/service-sms/src/transports/index.ts` declares `SMS_PROVIDER_SETTING_KEYS`.
- **This card:** `Fixes #22789` closed it `completed`. In this act, `pm:dispatched` and the assignee come off. `bug`, `domain:services`, `priority:p3` and `area:devpath` stay.
- **Outcome on record:**
  - a configured `twilio` or `aliyun` provider whose keys are in the environment (or in Settings) delivers without `OS_SMS_PROVIDER`;
  - a provider named in Settings or by `OS_SMS_PROVIDER` still wins;
  - a configured provider with no credentials anywhere still boots onto the log transport, with a warning and `isConfigured() === false`.
- **Carried forward:** #22748's landing record (`6107349646`) gates re-admitting `sms.provider` on the stack definition on this card. That gate is now met. The re-admission is a `domain:spec` card nobody has filed yet, and the seat relays the unlock to the `domain:spec` seat post. Two comments that become stale with this landing ride that card:
  - `packages/spec/src/system/sms-config.zod.ts`'s header says the SMS reader merges no environment credential into `providerOptions`;
  - `packages/cli/src/commands/serve-sms-capability.test.ts:68` says "Unlike mail, SMS credentials are not a boot-time input". They are now read at boot, but still not demanded.
- **Mis-close check:** PR #22815 names one closing target. No other lane card closed in the window. PR #22813 merged three minutes earlier as `Part of #22792`, and #22792 stays open.
